newsitem.title: USA: ISSUER FOCUS - Delaware County, Pa., IDA rev issue.
newsitem.headline: ISSUER FOCUS - Delaware County, Pa., IDA rev issue.

text.p: The Delaware County Industrial Authority, Pa., is expected to sell $231 million refunding bonds Wednesday in conjunction with Browning-Ferris Industries Inc's plan to acquire a waste-to-energy facility in Chester, Pa.
Goldman Sachs & Co is senior manager on the bond offering.
The offering, according to the preliminary statement, is structured with $102 million of serial bonds maturing in 1998 through 2009.
Also included in the deal are two term bonds: A 2031 maturity with $86 million of the offering and a 2032 maturity with $43 million of the issue.

The plant will be the sixth such facility managed by the American Ref-Fuel Company, a roughly 11-year-old joint venture between Browning-Ferris and Air Products & Chemicals, Stephen Simmons, a business manager at American Ref-Fuel said. BFI is based in Houston, Texas, while Air Products is located in Allentown, Pa.
"Each of the six plants has its own equity structure, and all the other five are 50-50 BFI and Air Products," Simmons said. "This is going to be a unique one, it's going to be 100 percent BFI."
The Chester plant is "part of our growth strategy of acquiring facilities," Simmons said.
The current true equity owner of the facility is General Electric Credit Corp, he said.
Westinghouse Electric Company built the plant, sold it to General Electric, and leased it back. BFI is purchasing the approximately 23-year lease hold interest from Westinghouse, Simmons said.
The facility can process 2,688 tons of solid waste per day on average. In terms of megawatts of electricity generated and sold, the facility generates 80 megawatts per hour, he said.
Simmons said he believed construction began on the plant in 1988, with the plant commencing commercial operations in 1991.
Though the resource recovery sector has come under pressure since the Supreme Court threw out flow-control ordinances in 1994, Simmons said the Chester plant has never had to rely on flow control.
"It's been a merchant plant since the beginning, so we get the market price of tipping fees in the Philadelphia area," he said, adding that those fees are generally in the $45 per ton range.
"We have some municipal contracts, but those are not necessarily tied to flow control ordinances," Simmons said.
Adam Matlawski, solicitor for the Delaware County IDA, said the county welcomes the acquisition.

"We have a company in here that has some good ideas and really wants to operate this plant," Matlawski said. "And the county does have a contract with this plant, so not just from an economic development standpoint, but also as a user, we are happy to see it."
